description:
New workspace member: `jmap-testjig`, a deliberately-minimal binary crate that wires the workspace's pieces (dispatcher + 8 extension handlers + reference MemoryBackends) into a running HTTP/SSE/WS process for the workspace's own integration testing and demonstration.

## NOT a product

`jmap-testjig` is published-false. It never goes to crates.io. It is not a JMAP server consumers should run. The workspace's identity remains 'library kit for building JMAP servers and clients in Rust'; the test jig is internal scaffolding for testing the kit, not a product layered on top.

## Constraints (absolute-minimal)

  - **Crate name**: `jmap-testjig`
  - **Directory**: `crate-jmap-testjig/`
  - **Cargo.toml**: `publish = false`. Single binary + library API for in-process test use.
  - **Transport**: axum + tokio-tungstenite. One choice, no matrix.
  - **Storage**: the 8 extension reference MemoryBackends, mounted.
  - **Auth**: hardcoded bearer token (e.g. `Authorization: Bearer test-token`). No OAuth, no JWT, no integration with anything.
  - **Bind**: localhost-only by default (`127.0.0.1:8080` say).
  - **Multi-tenancy**: none. Single hardcoded principal (e.g. `testuser@testjig.local`).
  - **Config**: none. All hardcoded. No env vars, no config file, no CLI flags beyond maybe `--port` and `--token`.
  - **Extensions wired up**: all 8 (mail, chat, calendars, tasks, contacts, filenode, sharing, metadata) at MVP. Configurable subset can come later if anyone needs it.
  - **Size target**: sub-1000 LoC for the MVP.
  - **Doc**: README + lib.rs module doc loudly state "NOT FOR PRODUCTION; in-memory only; single-user; no auth integration; no persistence".

## What it's good for

  - Workspace integration tests across the 6 client crates (replacing per-crate wiremock fixtures).
  - Smoke-test target: `cargo run -p jmap-testjig` and hit it with curl.
  - Contributor onboarding demo: "clone the repo, run the jig, see a working JMAP server".
  - Bug repro substrate.
  - Eventually, the in-process target for the JMAP-sc1b.17 examples that currently use wiremock+fixtures (.17.4 + .17.5).

## Suggested decomposition (child beads)

The following slices are the proposed shape; the autonomous loop or a future /do-beads pass may refine. Working order is roughly the listed order — slice 1 unblocks everything, slices 2-6 can interleave, slice 7 is the last to make sense.

  - **.1 — Scaffold**: `crate-jmap-testjig/` directory, Cargo.toml with `publish = false`, src/lib.rs, src/main.rs stub, dependency wiring (axum, tokio, tokio-tungstenite, all 8 workspace server crates + jmap-server foundation + reference MemoryBackends).

  - **.2 — Axum router**: `POST /jmap` dispatching through `jmap_server::Dispatcher`, `GET /.well-known/jmap` returning a hardcoded Session JSON with all 8 capabilities advertised.

  - **.3 — MemoryBackend wiring**: instantiate all 8 reference MemoryBackends, register their handler functions with the dispatcher, mount them at a single account-id under a single principal.

  - **.4 — SSE endpoint**: `GET /events` per RFC 8620 §7.3, streaming StateChange events from the MemoryBackends' change-tracking machinery.

  - **.5 — WebSocket endpoint**: `GET /ws` per RFC 8887, framing Request/Response and StateChange.

  - **.6 — Bearer auth middleware**: hardcoded token, axum middleware, 401 on mismatch.

  - **.7 — Integration test harness**: `pub fn spawn_in_process() -> (JoinHandle, SocketAddr)` helper so per-client-crate integration tests can spawn the jig and hit it without process management. Optionally a Drop guard to stop it.

  - **.8 — Doc + README**: NOT-FOR-PRODUCTION warnings, README explaining the test jig's role, contributor-facing usage notes.

## What this epic does NOT do

  - Add transport deps to any `*-server` crate. The server crates stay transport-less.
  - Add a MemoryBackend to `jmap-server` foundation. Foundation stays pure-dispatcher.
  - Implement PushSubscription (RFC 8620 §7.2). Deferred per JMAP-sc1b.107 (γ-deferred).
  - Migrate the .17.4 / .17.5 examples to use the test jig. Those ship via wiremock+fixtures (option A) regardless; migration is a future simplification.
  - Become a multi-tenant, configurable, auth-integrated server. Any pressure in that direction belongs in a separate consumer (kith, stoa) — not in the test jig.

## Acceptance

  - `cargo run -p jmap-testjig` spawns a working JMAP server on localhost.
  - JmapClient pointed at it can fetch Session, perform `Email/get`, `Mailbox/query`, `Chat/get`, `Space/set`, etc. across all 8 extensions.
  - At least one per-client-crate integration test uses `spawn_in_process` and hits the jig successfully.
  - `cargo test --workspace` clean (the jig is workspace-only; failures don't affect publish-readiness for the kit crates).
  - `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` clean.
  - All 8 children closed.

## Cross-references

  - JMAP-l99e — HTTP transport architectural epic, resolved by this epic (`*-server` crates stay transport-less; transport lives in jmap-testjig only).
  - JMAP-sc1b.17.4, .17.5 — examples currently using wiremock+fixtures; can migrate to test-jig after MVP lands.
  - JMAP-sc1b.107 — PushSubscription server-side (γ-deferred); test jig does not need it.
  - workspace AGENTS.md 'What this workspace is' section (to be added) — formalizes kit-plus-test-jig posture.
